title: Tooling: 5.36× faster production frameopt.close via one-basis modular closure with identical receipts
head: e45c48ca6b44b917d8114140a8715352667795ea
body:
## Change and scope

At base `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, production `research/bit589-frame-optimum/frameopt.py:close` still rebuilt a modular elimination for every candidate live line (`rank(S ∪ {L_i}) == rank(S)`). Ross Richardson’s opt-in adapter `research/bit-frame-closure-basis/` (incorporated [#1666](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1666)) already proved an equivalent one-basis membership test with identical PR589/PR555/degraded receipts. This PR wires that equivalent check into the **production** `close` used by `research/bit589-frame-optimum/verify.sh`.

No certificate κ pins change. The historical pairwise `frameopt.py` digest in `research/bit-frame-closure-basis/SOURCES.json` is demoted to **provenance** (and dropped from live `VERIFY.json` / `run.py` inputs) so research-packages CI does not fail working-source drift after the production rewrite. `research/r439-resynth-frame-seed10` still records the pairwise digest as certificate provenance and is left alone (no `VERIFY.json` / not in the research-packages matrix).

**Tooling improvement; no new kappa.** Selected frontier untouched.

## Result

On Linux / CPython 3.12.3 (Linux-6.12.94+-x86_64-with-glibc2.39), five alternating fresh-process pairs gave:

- PR589 median **17.298 → 3.213 s (5.38×)**
- Suite median (pr589+pr555+degraded) **47.744 → 8.904 s (5.36×)**

Timing is host-descriptive and is not a correctness gate. Every case receipt and stdout digest matches the baseline checker.

Package: `research/bit-frame-closure-production/`.
Tip: `e45c48ca6b44b917d8114140a8715352667795ea`.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/bit-frame-closure-production/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -B research/bit-frame-closure-production/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-frame-closure-production
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-frame-closure-basis --check-only
python3.12 -I -B research/bit-frame-closure-basis/verify.py
python3.12 -I -B research/bit-frame-closure-production/benchmark.py --rounds 5
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_BIT_FRAME_CLOSURE_PRODUCTION cases=['pr589', 'pr555', 'degraded'] corruption=subprocess_failure certs=0 no_new_kappa
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
PASS_BIT_FRAME_CLOSURE_BASIS
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/bit-frame-closure-production outcome=completed
PASS_IDENTICAL_BIT_FRAME_CLOSURE_PRODUCTION_RECEIPTS
```

Default verify is read-only. Temp-copy always-admit `_in_span` foil rejects via subprocess failure. Package gates under `-O` still launch assertion-enabled children. Full `make verify`, selected cold replay, Lean, and multiplication-theorem obligations were not rerun for this isolated checker change.

## Overlap and credit

Closest priors (different delivery): Ross Richardson’s `research/bit-frame-closure-basis/` / [#1666](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1666) (opt-in one-basis; this is the production wiring), [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#756](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/756), [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#2194](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2194) / [#2210](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2210) / [#2231](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2231) / [#2239](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2239) (same production-promotion pattern on other objects). No competing open PR on production `frameopt.close` at refresh.

Seth Burkart authored the PR886 frame-only optimum checker. Ross Richardson authored the one-basis algorithm. Prepared by Wentao Li ([VictorLiwentao](https://github.com/VictorLiwentao), [@Is__Victor](https://x.com/Is__Victor)) with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
